rationale: This is a product of two ranks of two well-known published anomalies (Cooper-Gulen-Schill asset growth and Bradshaw-Richardson-Sloan net external financing), and the claim that rank-multiplication "isolates the interaction rather than either main effect" is false — the product of two [0,1] ranks is dominated by the two main effects, so the test cannot distinguish the funding-source story from a simple composite of two known signals.

The conditional design is economically sensible and reasonably novel, but the hard indicator gate assigns exactly zero to roughly half the cross-section, piling mass at the median so quantile breakpoints degenerate and portfolio composition becomes unstable, and no ungated benchmark is included to establish that the leverage condition is what matters.

Stock-financed acquirer underperformance is a canonical published result (Loughran-Vijh, Rau-Vermaelen, plus net-share-issuance), and the expression is internally muddled because Compustat aqc records mainly the cash outflow for acquisitions — precisely what stock-financed deals lack — so the numerator mixes a cash-deal proxy with a goodwill proxy that partly double-counts it.

Beyond being a rescaled version of the known XFIN/net-external-financing anomaly, the construction is mechanically unsound: capx+aqc in the denominator is frequently near zero or zero, so extreme deciles will be populated by tiny-denominator firms rather than by the intended funding-mix contrast, and 1% winsorization will not repair a non-monotone ratio of two signed quantities.

This is essentially the multi-year composite-issuance/long-horizon-investment anomaly (Daniel-Titman; Bradshaw et al.) repackaged, and like the first proposal the rank product is driven by the two main effects rather than the claimed interaction, making it a cosmetic horizon variant of ExtFinFundedAssetGrowth rather than a distinct test.

Algebraically the signal reduces to RANK(investment) times a signed payout-minus-issuance rank difference, which is a defensible genuine interaction — investment intensity is differenced out and only funding mix is priced, with the expected positive sign matching the direction — though the bracket alone is close to a known net-payout-yield composite and prstkc appears in both legs, so the incremental content rests entirely on the investment gate and this should be benchmarked against the ungated funding-mix term.
